So this report presents proposed policy changes to support the creation of more on straight accessible parking spaces specific to our pay parking zones in commercial areas.

So the difference between the two types is the length of time that users may park in the associated space.
Accessible loading zones may only be used for up to 15 minutes while actively loading and unloading.
Where is accessible parking zones may be used for up to the area time limits typically three hours in downtown.
So the images on the right on the side show the signs used to designate each of these different spaces.
And we've identified that there is a suitable need for both types of parking spaces to exist in our pay parking zones since they do address different needs.
So in 2023 the city reviewed a successful parking permit program which resulted in public feedback about the lack of accessible parking on the street.
Particularly in our pay parking zones such as downtown and Broadway and Riversdale.
Residents also indicated that the design of these spaces were inadequate for user needs.
And it often there does still need to be a curb ramp associated with these spaces.
So there are several existing accessible parking options available to users in our pay parking areas.
However, they each come with their own challenges.
So the first option is utilizing off street parking in parking lots.
So while this option allows all day parking for users what we've heard is that the lots are often located too far from user destinations.
The second option is using loading zones on the street.
So while these are available to drivers displaying a provincial placard for up to the time limits of the area.
Loading zones do have high competition since they're available to all user groups and typically businesses rely on them for deliveries and that sort of thing.
Which leaves dedicated on street accessible parking areas.
Parking services did conduct an audit of these locations in the different pay parking zones which did confirm that there's not very many of them to meet demand.
And often we don't have a nearby curb ramp.
